name: libaco
workload: Pure context switch cost of libaco acosw versus libco coctx_swap, run in the same benchmark harness on one core.
claimed_speedup: acosw about 10.29 ns per switch (README on v1.0) versus libco coctx_swap 17.64 ns per switch (branch README); the branch README states '1.72x faster'
tradeoffs: Asymmetric C coroutines, x86-64 and i386 System V only; optional shared (copy) stacks; no scheduler or I/O layer; no Boost.Context comparison.
caveats: First-party numbers from 2018 on a cloud VM; compiler and flags not stated; the libco figure is on a separate branch that also reports a libco ABI bug; the two runs are on the same machine and date but different binaries. Last commit 2022.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'faster than libco context switch' and hnes/libaco branch tencent_libco_bug_report_and_coctx_swap_benchmark

name: minicoro
workload: Context switch, initialize and uninitialize cost in CPU cycles for the assembly backend versus the ucontext backend of the same library, pre-allocated coroutines.
claimed_speedup: Linux x86_64 context switch 9 cycles (assembly) versus 352 cycles (ucontext); initialize 31 versus 383 cycles
license: Unlicense OR MIT-0 (public domain or MIT No Attribution)
tradeoffs: Single-header C asymmetric coroutines; stack-per-coroutine memory; avoid C++ exceptions across switches; fiber and asyncify backends elsewhere.
caveats: Baseline is ucontext, not Boost.Context or libco; no cross-library comparison in the README; compiler and flags not stated. A third-party issue (PavelGuzenfeld/ucoro #11) measured a minicoro-derived x86-64 switch at about 3x Boost.Context before a return-mispredict fix, so it may not beat Boost.Context. Public domain / MIT-0 has no patent grant.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'stackful coroutine library C assembly context switch vs libco boost.context'

name: libcopp
workload: Single-coroutine switch overhead and 1000-coroutine creation and switch overhead for libcopp, libco, libgo and ucontext (64 KB stacks).
claimed_speedup: Single coroutine switch 77 ns (libcopp) vs 84 ns (libco static stack pool); 1000 coroutines switch 105 ns vs 168 ns; ucontext 439 ns and 505 ns. Creation at 1000 coroutines is 4.1 us vs 3.9 us (libco slightly faster).
tradeoffs: Stackful coroutines with stack pools, plus task layer (libcotask); uses Boost.Context-style fcontext assembly or ucontext; README points to CI output instead of numbers.
caveats: Benchmark is a 2019-09-29 gist by the libcopp author; CPU and OS not stated; gist shows libgo faster for a single coroutine (30 ns) and libcopp not faster at creation. README itself carries no numbers (links to CI output). Does not compare Boost.Context directly.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'coroutine library faster than libco' -> gist 'coroutine benckmark' by owent

name: libgo
workload: Same gist: stackful coroutine switch overhead, libgo with boost fcontext or ucontext backends versus libco, libcopp and ucontext.
claimed_speedup: Single coroutine switch 30 ns (libgo) vs 84 ns (libco static) vs 77 ns (libcopp); at 1000 coroutines libgo is 32 us vs libco 168 ns (slower)
tradeoffs: Full Go-style M:N scheduler with channels and syscall hooking; heavier than a bare context library; Boost.Context optional backend.
caveats: Mixed result: wins single-coroutine switch, loses at 1000 coroutines. Gist is by a competing library's author (libcopp), numbers 2019, CPU unstated. The libgo README shows only image graphs against Go.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'libco vs boost.context vs libgo vs coost' -> gist by owent

name: CO2
workload: Generator-style yield/resume cost: CO2 stackless emulated coroutines versus Boost.Coroutine2 versus native MSVC coroutines in test/benchmark.cpp.
claimed_speedup: CO2 6 ns versus Boost.Coroutine2 (bench_coroutine2) 82 ns, native MSVC 5 ns (about 13.7x, derived from page data)
tradeoffs: Stackless (macro-based) emulation, not stackful: no yielding from nested calls; needs Boost; superseded by the author's COZ; archived 2024-10-09.
caveats: Stackless versus Boost.Coroutine2's stackful switch, so not like for like; CPU not stated; VS2015-era numbers; repository archived. Last commit date not read (archived 2024-10-09).
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'C++ coroutine faster than boost Coroutine2 benchmark' -> jamboree/co2

name: TurboRoutine
workload: Round-trip resume plus yield cost for hand-written x86-64 assembly switch versus swapcontext and kernel thread handoff.
claimed_speedup: About 30 ns round trip vs about 2 us for ucontext (about 70x) and about 83 us for kernel thread handoff
tradeoffs: x86-64 Linux only; GPL-3.0; stack-pointer auto-discovery; 11 commits.
caveats: Does not compare Boost.Context or libco (README says so); a 30 ns round trip is slower than Boost.Context's about 5-6 ns on modern CPUs reported elsewhere; WSL2 laptop CPU; tiny project. Included as a documented off-baseline entry.
found_via: GitHub: WebSearch 'fcontext fast user-space context switch library benchmark'
